subject: Urgent: Elevated 5xx/429 after model rollout impacting checkout
messages:
From: Sara Ling <sara@brightlane.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, support@brightlane.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: High rate of 5xx/429 after model update — urgent

Hi Priya,

We pushed the new model variant (model-7b-quant-v2) to production in our account last night (approx 00:45 PDT). Since ~07:30 this morning we are seeing a sharp increase in 5xx responses and 429 throttles from the Redwood endpoint used by our checkout flow. Consumers are seeing timeouts (up to 10s) and clients are aggressively retrying — traffic on our side has spiked with client retries and it's causing cascading failures downstream (payment gateway failures).

Attached is a small sample of 429/5xx headers and a few request/response pairs. Key facts:
- Endpoint: /v1/generate (model pinned to model-7b-quant-v2)
- Error mix: ~60% 429s from Redwood, ~30% 5xx; timeouts otherwise
- First observed ~07:30 PDT (we had steady traffic overnight)

This is P1 for us — can you confirm receipt and advise immediate mitigation options? If rollback to previous model variant is possible please do so; otherwise tell us what you need to triage. We are open to an emergency call.

Thanks,
Sara Ling
CTO, Brightlane

Attachment: brightlane-429-sample.log (200KB)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Sara Ling <sara@brightlane.ai>, support@brightlane.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High rate of 5xx/429 after model update — urgent

Thanks Sara — received and escalating.

Action so far (T+25m):
- I’ve looped in Neha and the SRE/serving team to triage kernel/quant issues.
- Opening an incident: INC-20270402-BL-01 (link below).
- Proposed immediate mitigations: rollback to model-7b-quant-v1 or reduce batch_size / disable the new quant profile for Brightlane while we investigate.

Neha — can you pull perf traces and memory/CPU traces for the last 2 hours? The customer attached a sample log (brightlane-429-sample.log). We need a direct recommendation for rollback vs config tweak.

I’ll coordinate the customer P1 call at 09:00 PDT unless you recommend otherwise. Monica — please prep a one-page impact note for the account and confirm the service credit policy we may need to offer if SLA is hit.

Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0182

Related: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20270402-BL-01
Attachment: customer-impact-summary.pdf

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, monica_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Sara Ling <sara@brightlane.ai>, support@brightlane.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:54:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High rate of 5xx/429 after model update — urgent

On Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 8:37 AM PDT Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Neha — can you pull perf traces and memory/CPU traces for the last 2 hours?

I pulled traces and an initial heap snapshot. Quick summary of findings (T+42m):
- Symptoms: abrupt increase in token latency variance and kernel OOM spikes when the quantized kernels hit a specific attention pattern (long prefix + many open sessions).
- Root hypothesis: a quantization-profile mismatch in model-7b-quant-v2 combined with an updated kernel selection path caused transient cache eviction thrashing on the GPU device (observed at 07:28–07:42 PDT). That leads to delayed response scheduling and the fronting LB returning 429s under backlog.
- Evidence: repeated kernel-load/release in perf trace, elevated device mem_alloc churn, and ~3x increase in request latency p95→p99. See perf-trace-20270402.zip attached.

Immediate recommendation (ranked):
1) Rollback Brightlane to model-7b-quant-v1 for their production route (fastest, lowest-risk).
2) If rollback not possible now: set route-level override to reduce max_batch_size to 1 and disable the new kernel selector for that route. This reduces throughput but should remove the eviction pattern.
3) Collect longer traces (I need full model load logs and the customer’s request sample for the problematic session IDs).

I can start rollback/route override once I have a +1 from Priya/ops. If you want, we can do a partial rollback (pin only the hot path) and run a quick smoke test.

Neha Kapoor
SRE, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachments: perf-trace-20270402.zip, heap-snap-0728.txt

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, Sara Ling <sara@brightlane.ai>, support@brightlane.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: Immediate exec attention requested — Brightlane production outage (model regression)

Marissa / Jonas — heads up, Brightlane (strategic mid-market account; BL-2026-347) is experiencing a production outage after we rolled model-7b-quant-v2. Neha’s triage points to a quant/kernel interaction causing device churn and a backlog that surfaces as 429s and 5xx errors.

Customer impact summary:
- Checkout conversion impacted for ~30% of requests to their Redwood endpoint between 07:30–10:20 PDT.
- Payment gateway retries observed on their side; risk of lost transactions.
- Customer expects a P1 response and asked for rollback or credits.

Requesting the following from leadership:
- Approve immediate rollback to model-7b-quant-v1 for Brightlane production route (Neha recommends rollback as lowest-risk).
- Authorize us to offer a proactive service credit if SLA thresholds are crossed (Monica will propose the credit).
- Support an incident war room for the postmortem; will need product and research to join to re-evaluate the quantization profile and kernel selector logic.

I’ll hold the 09:00 PDT customer call; Neha will act on rollback once leadership confirms.

Thanks,
Priya

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Ling <sara@brightlane.ai>, support@brightlane.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Update: Rollback complete, metrics returned to baseline (Brightlane)

Quick update (post-call notes):
- Rollback to model-7b-quant-v1 executed at 10:22 PDT for the Brightlane prod route. Neha performed the route pin and validated a smoke test against their checkout flow.
- Observed behavior: p95/p99 latencies dropped back to baseline within ~10 minutes; 429 rate returned to <1% by 10:35 PDT. 5xx volume reduced to near-zero.
- Customer response: Sara reported that their checkout volume stabilized and they will pause automated client retries for 2 hours while we confirm stability. Customer asked for a written impact summary and a proposed timeline for a safe re-test of quant-v2.

Next steps:
- Postmortem draft (attached) — will schedule incident review with Product/Research to look at quant-profile v2 and kernel selector safety checks.
- Action items assigned: Neha to run regression tests with longer prefixes and larger session counts; Research to produce a mitigations list for the kernel selector; Priya/Monica to draft the customer credit offer and follow up on business impact.

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

Attachments: postmortem-draft.md, perf-summary.csv
Related link: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/cs/brightlane/2027-04-02/impact-report.pdf
